```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/course_helpers.R")
```

::: objectives
::: en
#### What this session is for
No new concepts here: six independent exercises to **practise** what you learned in Sessions 2 to 8, before the final project. Each exercise has its own quiz (**two attempts**, the best one counts) and its own solution, opened when you have used your attempts or got full marks. The final project opens when the six exercises together reach 75 % of their points.

- Do them in order or in any order; each starts by importing its data.
- Write everything in one script `scripts/s09_practice.R`, with one section per exercise (**Ctrl + Shift + R**).
- If you get less than 70 % on an exercise, re-read the session indicated before moving on.
:::
::: fr
#### À quoi sert cette séance
Pas de nouvelle notion ici : six exercices indépendants pour **pratiquer** ce que vous avez appris dans les séances 2 à 8, avant le projet final. Chaque exercice a son propre quiz (**deux tentatives**, la meilleure compte) et sa propre solution, ouverte quand vous avez utilisé vos tentatives ou obtenu tous les points. Le projet final s'ouvre quand les six exercices réunis atteignent 75 % de leurs points.

- Faites-les dans l'ordre ou non ; chacun commence par importer ses données.
- Écrivez tout dans un seul script `scripts/s09_practice.R`, avec une section par exercice (**Ctrl + Maj + R**).
- Si vous obtenez moins de 70 % à un exercice, relisez la séance indiquée avant de continuer.
:::
:::

```{r answers, include=FALSE}
sg   <- read.csv("data/seagrass_quadrats.csv")
fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")

# P1
p1a <- length(seq(1, 10, by = 0.75))
lab <- paste0("Q", rep(1:5, times = 3), "_", rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 5))
p1b <- lab[7]
set.seed(7); s7 <- sample(seq(0.5, 25, by = 0.5), 6)
p1c <- max(s7)
x <- c(12, 45, 7, 88, 23, 56)
p1d <- sort(x)[2]
p1e <- sum(rev(x)[1:2])

# P2
p2a <- sg[17, "species"]
p2b <- sum(sg[1:5, "seagrass_cover"])
p2c <- round(mean(sg[46:60, "shoot_density"]), 2)
sg2 <- sg; sg2$depth_m[sg2$depth_m < 0.6] <- 0.6
p2d <- round(mean(sg2$depth_m), 2)
p2e <- sum(is.na(sg$canopy_height_cm))

# P3
f3 <- fish
f3$biomass_kg <- f3$count * f3$a * f3$length_cm^f3$b / 1000
f3$n_per_ha <- f3$count / 250 * 10000
p3a <- sum(f3$count)
p3b <- round(max(f3$biomass_kg), 3)
p3c <- f3$n_per_ha[10]
f3 <- subset(f3, select = -c(family, a, b))
p3d <- ncol(f3)
p3e <- round(sapply(f3[, c("length_cm", "count", "biomass_kg")], mean)[["count"]], 2)

# P4
p4a <- nrow(subset(fish, mpa_status == "Outside" & species %in% c("Lutjanus kasmira", "Epinephelus merra")))
p4b <- ncol(subset(fish, length_cm > 25, select = site:species))
p4c <- round(mean(subset(fish, family == "Scaridae" & mpa_status == "Inside")$length_cm), 2)
xx <- c(" Ifaty", "ifaty", "IFATY ", "Mangily", "mangily ")
p4d <- length(unique(tools::toTitleCase(tolower(trimws(xx)))))
yy <- c("12", "15%", "-", "40", "8%")
yy <- gsub("%", "", yy); yy[yy == "-"] <- NA
p4e <- mean(as.numeric(yy), na.rm = TRUE)

# P5
f5 <- fish
f5$biomass_g <- f5$count * f5$a * f5$length_cm^f5$b
p5a <- tapply(f5$count, f5$site, sum)[["Ambola"]]
p5b <- round(aggregate(length_cm ~ mpa_status, data = f5, FUN = mean)$length_cm[1], 2)
p5c <- round(sd(f5$length_cm[f5$species == "Scarus ghobban"]), 2)
tr5 <- aggregate(biomass_g ~ mpa_status + site + transect, data = f5, FUN = sum)
tr5$kg_ha <- tr5$biomass_g / 1000 / 250 * 10000
p5d <- round(tapply(tr5$kg_ha, tr5$mpa_status, mean)[["Inside"]], 2)
out <- tr5$kg_ha[tr5$mpa_status == "Outside"]
p5e <- round(sd(out) / sqrt(length(out)), 2)

# P6
med6 <- tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$family, median)
p6a <- names(which.max(med6))
h6 <- hist(fish$length_cm, breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 5), plot = FALSE)
p6b <- max(h6$counts)
```

::: {.callout .ecology}
::: en
**Seagrass survey** (`seagrass_quadrats.csv`): in March 2026 a team of two snorkellers sampled **4 sites** (Ambalaboy and Fasimena inside a Marine Protected Area, Belitsaky and Tsiandamba outside), **15 quadrats of 50 × 50 cm** per site, placed every 5 m along a tape. For each quadrat they wrote on an underwater slate the depth (dive computer), the dominant species, the % cover (visual estimate), the canopy height (ruler, cm) and the number of shoots, converted to shoots per m². *Type:* one row = one quadrat; numeric (continuous) and categorical variables.

**Reef fish census** (`fish_uvc.csv`): underwater visual census on **4 reefs** (Andavaka and Belavenoke inside the MPA, Ambola and Tsifota outside), **3 belt transects of 50 × 5 m** (250 m²) per reef. A diver swam each transect and recorded every group of fish: species, family, estimated total length (cm) and number of individuals. The length–weight parameters `a` and `b` were added afterwards from FishBase. *Type:* one row = one group of fish of the same species and size; counts (integers), lengths (continuous), categories.
:::
::: fr
**Suivi des herbiers** (`seagrass_quadrats.csv`) : en mars 2026, une équipe de deux plongeurs en apnée a échantillonné **4 sites** (Ambalaboy et Fasimena dans une Aire Marine Protégée, Belitsaky et Tsiandamba à l'extérieur), **15 quadrats de 50 × 50 cm** par site, posés tous les 5 m le long d'un ruban. Pour chaque quadrat ils ont noté sur une ardoise la profondeur (ordinateur de plongée), l'espèce dominante, le % de recouvrement (estimation visuelle), la hauteur de canopée (règle, cm) et le nombre de pousses, converti en pousses par m². *Type :* une ligne = un quadrat ; variables numériques (continues) et catégorielles.

**Comptage des poissons récifaux** (`fish_uvc.csv`) : comptage visuel sous-marin sur **4 récifs** (Andavaka et Belavenoke dans l'AMP, Ambola et Tsifota à l'extérieur), **3 transects-bandes de 50 × 5 m** (250 m²) par récif. Un plongeur a parcouru chaque transect en notant chaque groupe de poissons : espèce, famille, longueur totale estimée (cm) et nombre d'individus. Les paramètres taille–poids `a` et `b` ont été ajoutés ensuite depuis FishBase. *Type :* une ligne = un groupe de poissons de même espèce et de même taille ; effectifs (entiers), longueurs (continues), catégories.
:::
:::

`r dl("seagrass_quadrats.csv", "seagrass_quadrats.csv")` `r dl("fish_uvc.csv", "fish_uvc.csv")`

## [Exercise 1 — Building vectors]{.en}[Exercice 1 — Créer des vecteurs]{.fr} {#ex1}

::: en
*Revise: Session 2.*

1. How many values does `seq(1, 10, by = 0.75)` contain?
2. Build `labels <- paste0("Q", rep(1:5, times = 3), "_", rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 5))`. What is `labels[7]`?
3. Run `set.seed(7)`, then draw 6 PIT positions with `sample(seq(0.5, 25, by = 0.5), 6)`. What is the largest position drawn?
4. With `x <- c(12, 45, 7, 88, 23, 56)`: what is the **second smallest** value (use `sort()`)?
5. What is the sum of the first two values of `rev(x)`?
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séance 2.*

1. Combien de valeurs contient `seq(1, 10, by = 0.75)` ?
2. Créez `labels <- paste0("Q", rep(1:5, times = 3), "_", rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 5))`. Que vaut `labels[7]` ?
3. Lancez `set.seed(7)`, puis tirez 6 positions PIT avec `sample(seq(0.5, 25, by = 0.5), 6)`. Quelle est la plus grande position tirée ?
4. Avec `x <- c(12, 45, 7, 88, 23, 56)` : quelle est la **deuxième plus petite** valeur (utilisez `sort()`) ?
5. Quelle est la somme des deux premières valeurs de `rev(x)` ?
:::

::: hint
::: en
`seq()` includes the start value; count with `length()`. In `paste0()`, `rep(1:5, times = 3)` repeats the whole series, `rep(..., each = 5)` repeats each value.
:::
::: fr
`seq()` inclut la valeur de départ ; comptez avec `length()`. Dans `paste0()`, `rep(1:5, times = 3)` répète toute la série, `rep(..., each = 5)` répète chaque valeur.
:::
:::

```{r quizp1, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p1", list(
  q_num("1. Number of values?", "1. Nombre de valeurs ?", p1a, tol = 0),
  q_text("2. labels[7]?", "2. labels[7] ?", p1b),
  q_num("3. Largest position drawn?", "3. Plus grande position tirée ?", p1c, tol = 0),
  q_num("4. Second smallest value?", "4. Deuxième plus petite valeur ?", p1d, tol = 0),
  q_num("5. Sum of the first two values of rev(x)?", "5. Somme des deux premières valeurs de rev(x) ?", p1e, tol = 0),
  q_mcq("6. What does seq(0, 1, length.out = 5) return?", "6. Que renvoie seq(0, 1, length.out = 5) ?",
        c("0 1 2 3 4", "0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8", "0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1", "1 2 3 4 5"), correct = 3)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 1", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 1")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p1"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
length(seq(1, 10, by = 0.75))            # 1
labels <- paste0("Q", rep(1:5, times = 3), "_", rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 5))
labels[7]                                 # 2. "Q2_B": 7th number is 2, 7th letter is B
set.seed(7)
s <- sample(seq(0.5, 25, by = 0.5), 6)
max(s)                                    # 3
x <- c(12, 45, 7, 88, 23, 56)
sort(x)[2]                                # 4
sum(rev(x)[1:2])                          # 5. rev(x) starts with 56, 23
```
:::

## [Exercise 2 — Addresses in a data frame]{.en}[Exercice 2 — Adresses dans un data frame]{.fr} {#ex2}

::: en
*Revise: Sessions 3 and 4.* Data: `sg <- read.csv("data/seagrass_quadrats.csv")`.

1. Which species is in row 17?
2. Sum of `seagrass_cover` in rows 1 to 5 (one line with `[row, column]`).
3. Rows 46 to 60 are the Belitsaky quadrats. Mean `shoot_density` of these rows (2 decimals).
4. The depth gauge cannot read below 0.6 m. On a copy `sg2`, replace every depth below 0.6 by 0.6. Mean depth afterwards (2 decimals)?
5. How many values of `canopy_height_cm` are missing?
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séances 3 et 4.* Données : `sg <- read.csv("data/seagrass_quadrats.csv")`.

1. Quelle espèce se trouve à la ligne 17 ?
2. Somme de `seagrass_cover` sur les lignes 1 à 5 (une seule ligne avec `[ligne, colonne]`).
3. Les lignes 46 à 60 sont les quadrats de Belitsaky. Moyenne de `shoot_density` sur ces lignes (2 décimales).
4. La sonde ne lit pas en dessous de 0,6 m. Sur une copie `sg2`, remplacez toute profondeur inférieure à 0,6 par 0,6. Profondeur moyenne ensuite (2 décimales) ?
5. Combien de valeurs de `canopy_height_cm` sont manquantes ?
:::

::: hint
::: en
Question 2: `sum(sg[1:5, "seagrass_cover"])`. Question 4: `sg2 <- sg`, then `sg2$depth_m[sg2$depth_m < 0.6] <- 0.6`.
:::
::: fr
Question 2 : `sum(sg[1:5, "seagrass_cover"])`. Question 4 : `sg2 <- sg`, puis `sg2$depth_m[sg2$depth_m < 0.6] <- 0.6`.
:::
:::

```{r quizp2, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p2", list(
  q_text("1. Species in row 17?", "1. Espèce de la ligne 17 ?", p2a),
  q_num("2. Sum of cover in rows 1 to 5?", "2. Somme du recouvrement lignes 1 à 5 ?", p2b, tol = 0),
  q_num("3. Mean shoot density, rows 46 to 60 (2 decimals)?", "3. Densité moyenne, lignes 46 à 60 (2 décimales) ?", p2c, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("4. Mean depth after the correction (2 decimals)?", "4. Profondeur moyenne après correction (2 décimales) ?", p2d, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("5. Number of missing canopy heights?", "5. Nombre de hauteurs de canopée manquantes ?", p2e, tol = 0),
  q_mcq("6. What does sg[3, ] return?", "6. Que renvoie sg[3, ] ?",
        c("Column 3", "Row 3, all columns", "The value in row 3, column 3", "The first 3 rows"),
        c("La colonne 3", "La ligne 3, toutes les colonnes", "La valeur ligne 3, colonne 3", "Les 3 premières lignes"), correct = 2)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 2", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 2")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p2"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
sg <- read.csv("data/seagrass_quadrats.csv")
sg[17, "species"]                                   # 1
sum(sg[1:5, "seagrass_cover"])                      # 2
round(mean(sg[46:60, "shoot_density"]), 2)          # 3
sg2 <- sg
sg2$depth_m[sg2$depth_m < 0.6] <- 0.6               # 4. condition inside [ ]
round(mean(sg2$depth_m), 2)
sum(is.na(sg$canopy_height_cm))                     # 5
```
:::

## [Exercise 3 — Columns from calculations]{.en}[Exercice 3 — Colonnes calculées]{.fr} {#ex3}

::: en
*Revise: Session 4.* Data: `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")`. Transect area = 250 m².

1. Total number of fish observed (sum of `count`).
2. Add `biomass_kg` = count × a × length_cm^b / 1000. What is the largest value of `biomass_kg` (3 decimals)?
3. Add `n_per_ha` = count / 250 × 10000 (fish per hectare). Value in row 10?
4. Remove the columns `family`, `a` and `b` in one line with `subset(..., select = -c(...))`. How many columns are left?
5. With `sapply()` on `length_cm`, `count` and `biomass_kg`, compute the mean of each column. Mean of `count` (2 decimals)?
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séance 4.* Données : `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")`. Surface d'un transect = 250 m².

1. Nombre total de poissons observés (somme de `count`).
2. Ajoutez `biomass_kg` = count × a × length_cm^b / 1000. Quelle est la plus grande valeur de `biomass_kg` (3 décimales) ?
3. Ajoutez `n_per_ha` = count / 250 × 10000 (poissons par hectare). Valeur à la ligne 10 ?
4. Supprimez les colonnes `family`, `a` et `b` en une ligne avec `subset(..., select = -c(...))`. Combien de colonnes reste-t-il ?
5. Avec `sapply()` sur `length_cm`, `count` et `biomass_kg`, calculez la moyenne de chaque colonne. Moyenne de `count` (2 décimales) ?
:::

::: hint
::: en
`^` is computed before `*`: `fish$count * fish$a * fish$length_cm^fish$b / 1000`. For question 5, `sapply(fish[, c("length_cm", "count", "biomass_kg")], mean)`.
:::
::: fr
`^` est calculé avant `*` : `fish$count * fish$a * fish$length_cm^fish$b / 1000`. Pour la question 5, `sapply(fish[, c("length_cm", "count", "biomass_kg")], mean)`.
:::
:::

```{r quizp3, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p3", list(
  q_num("1. Total number of fish?", "1. Nombre total de poissons ?", p3a, tol = 0),
  q_num("2. Largest biomass_kg (3 decimals)?", "2. Plus grande biomass_kg (3 décimales) ?", p3b, tol = 0.0006),
  q_num("3. n_per_ha in row 10?", "3. n_per_ha à la ligne 10 ?", p3c, tol = 0.01),
  q_num("4. Number of columns left?", "4. Nombre de colonnes restantes ?", p3d, tol = 0),
  q_num("5. Mean of count (2 decimals)?", "5. Moyenne de count (2 décimales) ?", p3e, tol = 0.006),
  q_mcq("6. Which line adds a column to fish?", "6. Quelle ligne ajoute une colonne à fish ?",
        c("fish[\"new\"] == 1", "fish$new <- 1", "new(fish) <- 1", "fish <- fish + new"), correct = 2)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 3", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 3")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p3"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")
sum(fish$count)                                                  # 1
fish$biomass_kg <- fish$count * fish$a * fish$length_cm^fish$b / 1000
round(max(fish$biomass_kg), 3)                                   # 2
fish$n_per_ha <- fish$count / 250 * 10000
fish[10, "n_per_ha"]                                             # 3
fish <- subset(fish, select = -c(family, a, b))
ncol(fish)                                                       # 4
sapply(fish[, c("length_cm", "count", "biomass_kg")], mean)      # 5
```
:::

::: {.callout .try}
::: en
**Try it.** Before Exercise 4: with `subset()`, keep the fish of more than 25 cm **inside** the MPA and only the columns `site`, `species` and `length_cm`. How many rows?
:::
::: fr
**À vous.** Avant l'exercice 4 : avec `subset()`, gardez les poissons de plus de 25 cm **dans** l'AMP et seulement les colonnes `site`, `species` et `length_cm`. Combien de lignes ?

## [Exercise 4 — `subset()` and cleaning]{.en}[Exercice 4 — `subset()` et nettoyage]{.fr} {#ex4}

::: en
*Revise: Session 5.* Data: re-import `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")` (Exercise 3 removed some columns).

1. How many rows are snappers or groupers (`Lutjanus kasmira` or `Epinephelus merra`, use `%in%`) **outside** the MPA?
2. How many columns does `subset(fish, length_cm > 25, select = site:species)` keep?
3. Mean length of parrotfish (`family == "Scaridae"`) **inside** the MPA (2 decimals).
4. Clean `x <- c(" Ifaty", "ifaty", "IFATY ", "Mangily", "mangily ")` with `trimws()`, `tolower()` and `tools::toTitleCase()`. How many different values remain?
5. Clean `y <- c("12", "15%", "-", "40", "8%")`: remove `%`, turn `"-"` into `NA`, convert to numbers. Mean of `y` without NA?
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séance 5.* Données : réimportez `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")` (l'exercice 3 a supprimé des colonnes).

1. Combien de lignes sont des vivaneaux ou des mérous (`Lutjanus kasmira` ou `Epinephelus merra`, utilisez `%in%`) **hors** AMP ?
2. Combien de colonnes garde `subset(fish, length_cm > 25, select = site:species)` ?
3. Taille moyenne des poissons-perroquets (`family == "Scaridae"`) **dans** l'AMP (2 décimales).
4. Nettoyez `x <- c(" Ifaty", "ifaty", "IFATY ", "Mangily", "mangily ")` avec `trimws()`, `tolower()` et `tools::toTitleCase()`. Combien de valeurs différentes reste-t-il ?
5. Nettoyez `y <- c("12", "15%", "-", "40", "8%")` : retirez `%`, transformez `"-"` en `NA`, convertissez en nombres. Moyenne de `y` sans NA ?
:::

::: hint
::: en
Question 1: `fish$species %in% c("Lutjanus kasmira", "Epinephelus merra") & fish$mpa_status == "Outside"`, then `sum()`.
:::
::: fr
Question 1 : `fish$species %in% c("Lutjanus kasmira", "Epinephelus merra") & fish$mpa_status == "Outside"`, puis `sum()`.
:::
:::

```{r quizp4, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p4", list(
  q_num("1. Snapper or grouper rows outside the MPA?", "1. Lignes de vivaneaux ou mérous hors AMP ?", p4a, tol = 0),
  q_num("2. Number of columns kept?", "2. Nombre de colonnes gardées ?", p4b, tol = 0),
  q_num("3. Mean length of Scaridae inside (2 decimals)?", "3. Taille moyenne des Scaridae dans l'AMP (2 décimales) ?", p4c, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("4. Different values after cleaning?", "4. Valeurs différentes après nettoyage ?", p4d, tol = 0),
  q_num("5. Mean of y?", "5. Moyenne de y ?", p4e, tol = 0.006),
  q_mcq("6. Inside subset(), how do you write the column cover?", "6. Dans subset(), comment écrit-on la colonne cover ?",
        c("df$cover", "cover", "\"df$cover\"", "[cover]"), correct = 2)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 4", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 4")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p4"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")
nrow(subset(fish, mpa_status == "Outside" &
                  species %in% c("Lutjanus kasmira", "Epinephelus merra")))     # 1
ncol(subset(fish, length_cm > 25, select = site:species))                     # 2
round(mean(subset(fish, family == "Scaridae" & mpa_status == "Inside")$length_cm), 2)  # 3
x <- c(" Ifaty", "ifaty", "IFATY ", "Mangily", "mangily ")
length(unique(tools::toTitleCase(tolower(trimws(x)))))                       # 4
y <- c("12", "15%", "-", "40", "8%")
y <- gsub("%", "", y)
y[y == "-"] <- NA
mean(as.numeric(y), na.rm = TRUE)                                            # 5
```
:::

## [Exercise 5 — Statistics per group]{.en}[Exercice 5 — Statistiques par groupe]{.fr} {#ex5}

::: en
*Revise: Session 6.* Data: `fish`, with a column `biomass_g` = count × a × length_cm^b.

1. Total number of fish counted at Ambola (`tapply()` with `sum`).
2. Mean `length_cm` inside the MPA with `aggregate(length_cm ~ mpa_status, ...)` (2 decimals).
3. SD of `length_cm` for *Scarus ghobban* (2 decimals).
4. **Two steps.** (a) Total biomass **per transect**: `aggregate(biomass_g ~ mpa_status + site + transect, data = fish, FUN = sum)`. (b) Convert to kg/ha (÷ 1000, ÷ 250, × 10000). (c) Mean kg/ha of the **Inside** transects (2 decimals)?
5. SE of the kg/ha of the **Outside** transects (2 decimals)?
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séance 6.* Données : `fish`, avec une colonne `biomass_g` = count × a × length_cm^b.

1. Nombre total de poissons comptés à Ambola (`tapply()` avec `sum`).
2. Moyenne de `length_cm` dans l'AMP avec `aggregate(length_cm ~ mpa_status, ...)` (2 décimales).
3. ET de `length_cm` pour *Scarus ghobban* (2 décimales).
4. **Deux étapes.** (a) Biomasse totale **par transect** : `aggregate(biomass_g ~ mpa_status + site + transect, data = fish, FUN = sum)`. (b) Convertir en kg/ha (÷ 1000, ÷ 250, × 10000). (c) Moyenne des kg/ha des transects **Inside** (2 décimales) ?
5. ES des kg/ha des transects **Outside** (2 décimales) ?
:::

::: hint
::: en
Question 4: after `aggregate()`, the result has one row per transect (12 rows). Convert with `/ 1000 / 250 * 10000`, then use `tapply()` on that table.
:::
::: fr
Question 4 : après `aggregate()`, le résultat a une ligne par transect (12 lignes). Convertissez avec `/ 1000 / 250 * 10000`, puis utilisez `tapply()` sur ce tableau.
:::
:::

```{r quizp5, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p5", list(
  q_num("1. Total fish counted at Ambola?", "1. Total de poissons comptés à Ambola ?", p5a, tol = 0),
  q_num("2. Mean length inside the MPA (2 decimals)?", "2. Taille moyenne dans l'AMP (2 décimales) ?", p5b, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("3. SD of length of Scarus ghobban (2 decimals)?", "3. ET de la taille de Scarus ghobban (2 décimales) ?", p5c, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("4. Mean kg/ha of the Inside transects (2 decimals)?", "4. Moyenne des kg/ha des transects Inside (2 décimales) ?", p5d, tol = 0.006),
  q_num("5. SE of kg/ha of the Outside transects (2 decimals)?", "5. ES des kg/ha des transects Outside (2 décimales) ?", p5e, tol = 0.006),
  q_mcq("6. Why compute biomass per transect before averaging?", "6. Pourquoi calculer la biomasse par transect avant de faire la moyenne ?",
        c("Because R cannot sum rows", "Because the transect is the sampling unit (replicate)",
          "To get more decimals", "It makes no difference"),
        c("Parce que R ne sait pas additionner des lignes", "Parce que le transect est l'unité d'échantillonnage (réplicat)",
          "Pour avoir plus de décimales", "Cela ne change rien"), correct = 2)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 5", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 5")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p5"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")
fish$biomass_g <- fish$count * fish$a * fish$length_cm^fish$b
tapply(fish$count, fish$site, sum)                                  # 1
aggregate(length_cm ~ mpa_status, data = fish, FUN = mean)          # 2
round(sd(fish$length_cm[fish$species == "Scarus ghobban"]), 2)      # 3
tr <- aggregate(biomass_g ~ mpa_status + site + transect, data = fish, FUN = sum)
tr$kg_ha <- tr$biomass_g / 1000 / 250 * 10000
round(tapply(tr$kg_ha, tr$mpa_status, mean), 2)                     # 4
out <- tr$kg_ha[tr$mpa_status == "Outside"]
round(sd(out) / sqrt(length(out)), 2)                               # 5. n = 6 transects
```
:::

## [Exercise 6 — Graphs and equivalences]{.en}[Exercice 6 — Graphiques et équivalences]{.fr} {#ex6}

::: en
*Revise: Sessions 7 and 8.* Data: re-import `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")` (Exercise 3 removed some columns).

1. Draw `boxplot(length_cm ~ family, data = fish, las = 2)`. Which family has the **highest median** length?
2. Draw `h <- hist(fish$length_cm, breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 5))`. How many fish groups are in the most frequent size class (`h$counts`)?
3. Make the same boxplot with ggplot2.
4. Answer the questions on equivalences between base R and the tidyverse.
:::
::: fr
*Révision : séances 7 et 8.* Données : réimportez `fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")` (l'exercice 3 a supprimé des colonnes).

1. Tracez `boxplot(length_cm ~ family, data = fish, las = 2)`. Quelle famille a la **médiane** de taille **la plus élevée** ?
2. Tracez `h <- hist(fish$length_cm, breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 5))`. Combien de groupes de poissons se trouvent dans la classe de taille la plus fréquente (`h$counts`) ?
3. Faites le même boxplot avec ggplot2.
4. Répondez aux questions sur les équivalences entre R de base et le tidyverse.
:::

::: hint
::: en
For the medians of a boxplot without reading the graph: `sort(tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$family, median))`.
:::
::: fr
Pour les médianes d'un boxplot sans lire le graphique : `sort(tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$family, median))`.
:::
:::

```{r quizp6, echo=FALSE}
quiz("p6", list(
  q_text("1. Family with the highest median length?", "1. Famille à la médiane de taille la plus élevée ?", p6a),
  q_num("2. Number of groups in the most frequent class?", "2. Nombre de groupes dans la classe la plus fréquente ?", p6b, tol = 0),
  q_mcq("3. ggplot2 equivalent of par(mfrow = c(2, 2)) with one plot per site?", "3. Équivalent ggplot2 de par(mfrow = c(2, 2)) avec un graphique par site ?",
        c("facet_wrap(~ site)", "geom_col()", "theme_bw()", "labs(site)"), correct = 1),
  q_mcq("4. dplyr equivalent of tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$site, mean)?", "4. Équivalent dplyr de tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$site, mean) ?",
        c("fish |> filter(site) |> mean(length_cm)", "fish |> group_by(site) |> summarise(m = mean(length_cm))",
          "fish |> select(site, length_cm)", "fish |> mutate(m = mean(site))"), correct = 2),
  q_mcq("5. Base R equivalent of arrange(fish, desc(count))?", "5. Équivalent en R de base de arrange(fish, desc(count)) ?",
        c("sort(fish)", "fish[order(fish$count, decreasing = TRUE), ]", "fish[fish$count, ]", "rev(fish$count)"), correct = 2),
  q_mcq("6. Base R equivalent of ggsave()?", "6. Équivalent en R de base de ggsave() ?",
        c("write.csv()", "save()", "png() ... dev.off()", "print()"), correct = 3)
), title_en = "Quiz — Exercise 6", title_fr = "Quiz — Exercice 6")
```

::: {.solution data-quiz="p6"}
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fish <- read.csv("data/fish_uvc.csv")
boxplot(length_cm ~ family, data = fish, las = 2, xlab = "")
tapply(fish$length_cm, fish$family, median)          # 1: check the highest
h <- hist(fish$length_cm, breaks = seq(0, 40, by = 5))
h$counts; max(h$counts)                               # 2
library(ggplot2)                                      # 3
ggplot(fish, aes(family, length_cm)) + geom_boxplot() +
  theme_classic() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
:::
